title: How many guests can a Dubai caterer serve for one event?
body_html:
How many guests a Dubai caterer can serve is not a single city-wide number. It depends on the menu, service format, staffing, equipment and your venue. The useful figure is the guest count a caterer confirms for your particular event — not the largest event it has ever run.

If you are still shaping the occasion, start with catering in Dubai, then confirm capacity against the actual plan: menu, format, timetable and site.

Capacity is confirmed per event, not city-wide

Service formatWhat capacity depends onThe question to ask
Plated diningKitchen output, plating space and service staffHow do courses reach every table within the timetable?
BuffetServing space, queue flow and replenishmentWho maintains and replenishes the spread?
Canapé receptionTray circulation and food quantity per guestIs this a light reception or a dinner replacement?
Drop-offHandover, presentation and clearingWho serves and clears after the delivery?

No format removes the question by itself. A buffet still needs replenishment; a reception still needs food distributed across the room.

What changes the number

  • Menu complexity: which dishes need finishing or individual preparation at the venue.
  • Service format: seated, self-service or passed food.
  • Staffing: the proposed cooking, serving and clearing roles — a chef does not automatically cover every hosting task.
  • Kitchen and equipment: preparation surfaces, refrigeration and what is brought in.
  • Access and layout: delivery route, lifts, stairs and the distance from kitchen to guests.
  • Timetable: arrivals, speeches, meal service and any fixed finish.

A worked capacity check

For a hypothetical 40-guest villa dinner, the arithmetic looks like this: forty plated mains finished inside one service window need plating space, a finishing plan and enough service staff to carry the courses within the timetable. The same forty guests at a buffet need queue space and a replenishment rhythm instead. The headcount is identical; the operational plan is not. Treat a proposal as unconfirmed until it explains how your format and timetable work — these are planning considerations, not capacity promises.

What to send with the enquiry

  • Date, location and guest count, including children and organisers who need food.
  • The service format, or the experience you want if the format is undecided.
  • Meal timing and any fixed moments in the evening.
  • Dietary requirements, kept separate from preferences.
  • Kitchen, equipment and access details for the venue.

If the guest count changes

Treat an increase as a scope change that needs written acceptance. The caterer must confirm what the revised attendance means for food, staffing and equipment — an earlier capacity discussion does not guarantee later additions.

FAQ

Does a capacity statement include staff and equipment?

Do not assume it does. Request a proposal that identifies the people, serviceware and facilities included, and anything you must arrange separately.

Can one chef cater the whole event?

Confirm the full staffing plan rather than assuming one chef covers cooking, serving and clearing. The arrangement depends on menu, kitchen, guest count and service expectations.

Is a buffet better for a larger guest list?

A buffet offers guest choice; plated dining gives a coordinated seated meal. Neither establishes capacity by itself — check serving space, staffing and timing.

Should children count in the guest total?

Include everyone who needs food and distinguish adults from children, then ask how the caterer reflects those groups in the menu and confirmed attendance.

Related guides

Ask how the last guest is served

The question that settles capacity is how the last guest is served — not only how the food arrives. It brings preparation, service routes, staffing and timing into one conversation. For a tailored myCHEF catering enquiry, share your date, location, guest count and service required, then ask for written confirmation of the proposed capacity and responsibilities.
